hook: The teacher from Nazareth whose life and death gave rise to Christianity.

pages.x: The Gospels say Jesus was born in Bethlehem around 4 BC, in the reign of King Herod, to Mary, a young woman engaged to Joseph, a carpenter of Nazareth. He was laid in a manger because there was no room at the inn, and visited by shepherds and by wise men from the east who had followed a star.

He grew up in Nazareth in Galilee, probably working as a builder like Joseph. At about 30 he was baptised by his cousin John the Baptist in the River Jordan, and then, the Gospels say, spent forty days fasting in the desert.

He chose twelve disciples, several of them fishermen, and taught by the Sea of Galilee in parables, short stories like the Good Samaritan and the Prodigal Son. In the Sermon on the Mount he said: "Blessed are the meek", "Love your enemies" and "Do to others as you would have them do to you."

The Gospels tell of miracles: healing the blind and lepers, feeding 5,000 people with five loaves and two fish, walking on water and raising his friend Lazarus from the dead. Crowds followed him, and he shocked respectable people by eating with tax collectors, outcasts and the poor.

Around AD 30 he entered Jerusalem for the Passover festival, cheered by crowds waving palm branches, and overturned the tables of the money changers in the Temple. At a last meal with his disciples he shared bread and wine, and foretold that one of them would betray him.

Judas led the Temple guards to him at night in a garden. Accused of claiming to be king of the Jews, he was sentenced by the Roman governor, Pontius Pilate, and crucified outside the city walls between two thieves.

The Gospels say that on the third day his tomb was found empty, and that he appeared to his followers before rising into heaven. Christians celebrate the resurrection at Easter, the most important day of their year.

The faith his followers spread has grown into the largest religion in the world, with over two billion Christians. His teachings on love, forgiveness and care for the poor shaped Western art, law and ethics.
pts: The founder of Christianity, the world's largest religion
Taught love of enemies and the Golden Rule
Our calendar counts the years from his birth
